claim: Far-field examples raise novelty and the spread of idea quality in novice designers (d about 0.56 to 0.64 vs near) but cost about one idea fewer (d=-0.30).
agent_test: Give the agent a near vs far retrieved analogue before S3 at equal tokens; score novelty by code-run difference from baseline answers and count distinct candidates.

claim: The far-beats-near result does not generalise: Fu et al 2013 found far patents gave LOWER max novelty (d=-0.82 vs near, -0.91 vs control) and lower mean quality (d=-0.76) than near; the few studies with 18 or more per cell split evenly for and against far.
agent_test: Run both distances on the same task set; report the sign per task class rather than one pooled effect.

claim: A sweet spot of intermediate distance reconciles the 2011 and 2013 studies, but the account is post hoc and its location depends on the problem and the source set.
agent_test: Sweep analogue distance in 3 to 4 bins (embedding or graph distance) per task class and fit where success peaks; do not hard-code a bin.

claim: Less-common examples help and more-common examples hurt: common examples cut breadth (d=-1.03) and quantity (d=-0.76) vs control, fixating novices; only far plus less-common beat control on novelty.
agent_test: Compare common vs uncommon retrieved analogues; measure how many distinct solution families the attempts cover.

claim: Part of the quantity cost of far examples is mapping time, not lost ideas: the final-phase quantity effect vanished (p=.47).
agent_test: Charge analogue-mapping tokens to the budget; compare at equal total tokens, not equal attempts.

claim: In real innovation-contest data, using any cited inspiration is linked to expert shortlisting (16% of 707 citing concepts vs 10% of all 2341) while source distance adds little (AIC 511.4 to 505.1); in lab protocols, an analogy raises the odds that the next idea is creative (OR=1.99 lag 0). Both are correlational.
agent_test: Test whether adding an analogue step raises held-out pass rate relative to a resampling step with the same tokens; do not assume distance matters.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Humans retrieve by surface similarity but find only relational matches useful: 55% recall for surface-matched stories vs 12% for purely analogical matches (Gentner 1993, quoted second-hand); Gick-Holyoak about 10% unaided vs 41% with spontaneous use after a hint.
agent_test: Only secondary sources read; re-open Gentner 1993 first. Test retrieval by surface vs by typed structure on analogue banks.

claim: Comparing two cases side by side (analogical encoding) raised later use of the strategy about 3x in negotiation (Exp 2) and moved contingency use from 0% to 69% (Exp 1B).
agent_test: At S9, store lessons as compared pairs (two solved problems with the shared schema written out) vs single lessons; test transfer to fresh items.

claim: Structure-based analogy mining (purpose/mechanism vectors) produced more good ideas than random or TF-IDF surface retrieval: 46% vs 37% vs 30% (k=2, 9 shared seeds) and 38% vs 22% vs 21% (k=3, all 749 ideas); wide intervals and no replication.
agent_test: Retrieve analogues by abstracted purpose vector vs raw-text embedding; judge by held-out pass rate.

claim: Surface similarity pulls both humans and tools: SBERT alone scores 77.9% on near analogies in ARN but far analogies defeat models; in Hope et al.'s example the TF-IDF baseline returned same-domain items; GPT generators retrieved birds as the analogy in over 50% of cases for a flying-car task; and GPT-4 accuracy on story analogies fell when the correct story was paraphrased to remove sentence-level overlap with the source, suggesting it partly relies on that overlap.
agent_test: Force a rewrite to an abstract schema before retrieval; measure fraction of retrieved analogues from the same domain.
audit_note: SBERT 77.9% is a good score on near analogies (not a failure); TF-IDF same-domain is one figure caption on a single seed; the human claim rests on Hope et al. citing earlier work; Lewis and Mitchell show GPT-4 accuracy drops with paraphrase, suggesting rather than proving a sentence-overlap shortcut.
claim_before_audit: Surface-similarity retrieval is the default failure of both humans and tools: SBERT scores 77.9% on near analogies, TF-IDF returned same-domain items, an LLM retriever returned birds first for over 50% of cases, and GPT-4 uses sentence-level overlap as a shortcut.

claim: LLMs of 2022 to 2023 vintage do much worse on far than near analogies: GPT-3 far story p=.065 (n.s.) vs near p=.0039; ARN far analogies 39.6% (below 50% chance) vs near 75.0%, human 94.1% and 97.9%; StoryAnalogy best model 37.7 points below humans.
agent_test: Re-run the far/near split with the current model; if far is at chance, restrict O7 to code-checked mappings only.
audit_note: GPT-3 p-values (near sig, far n.s.) are not a direct near-vs-far test, and StoryAnalogy's 37.7-point human gap (abstract says 37.7%) is not a near/far comparison; the quoted numbers are correct.

claim: Whether LLM analogy is robust is contested: Webb et al report human-like performance in several domains, while Lewis and Mitchell find counterfactual letter-string accuracy 0.35 to 0.49 vs humans 0.753, answer-order bias (GPT-4 89% vs 61%), and a surface-overlap shortcut; paraphrase drops GPT-4 0.86 to 0.72. Update: with code execution GPT-4 matches humans on the counterfactual task (P=0.92, PNAS Nexus 2025), so much of the failure is a counting problem.
agent_test: Always test analogues on perturbed variants (counterfactual, reordered, paraphrased); treat unperturbed pass as no evidence.

claim: Prompting a model to recall self-generated related problems before solving gives small gains on maths (GSM8K 77.8 vs 75.8 0-shot CoT, GPT-3.5; MATH 37.3 vs 33.9) and larger gains on Codeforces and BIG-Bench; a second method (Thought Propagation) reports +12 to +15 points. Both are the authors own benchmarks, no independent replication. Update: margin over 5-shot CoT is only +1.1 (GSM8K) and +2.4 (MATH); self-consistency adds +7.5 and +8.7; recent strong models ignore CoT exemplars (Cheng 2026) and R1 degrades with few-shot.
agent_test: Add a recall-analogues step vs a same-token extra-sample baseline and vs 5-shot CoT; keep only if it wins (G7).

claim: Analogy generation quality scales with model size and prompt wording: meaningful share without a source 1.9% (0.3B), 15.6%, 48.3%, 70.05% (175B) vs human 66.67%; imperative low-temperature prompts best.
agent_test: Check on the current model; measure prompt wording sensitivity with 5 paraphrases.

claim: Prompt looseness trades novelty for feasibility in LLM-generated biologically inspired designs: loose prompts were more diverse and more novel, strict prompts more feasible (relevancy pass 62% to 80%); mirrors the human near/far trade-off.
agent_test: Vary how loosely the analogue constraint is stated; log novelty (code) and feasibility (check) together.

claim: One-shot example prompting makes GPT-3-era analogy suggestions more distant and more often unique and useful (unique-and-useful 0.43 zero-shot vs 0.70 to 0.77 one-shot); in use, 84% of analogies were added to the design, but a-priori usefulness did not predict in-use helpfulness (r=-0.027) and up to 25% could be harmful.
agent_test: Judge analogue value only by downstream run results; a model or one-rater usefulness rating is near-useless as a filter.

claim: LLM-generated research ideas are rated more novel than expert ones (5.64 vs 4.84, 79 reviewers) but are heavily redundant (about 5% of 4000 seeds non-duplicate) and the LLM cannot rank its own ideas.
agent_test: Deduplicate by code and select by execution; count unique candidates per token.

claim: Evidence that LLM design-by-analogy systems help real designers is thin: a survey of 85 studies reports a significant lack of rigorous empirical evaluation.
agent_test: Treat all published DbA-LLM gains as unproven; run our own equal-token control.

claim: On recent strong or reasoning models, exemplar-style prompting gives about zero gain over zero-shot: Qwen2.5 models ignore CoT exemplars on GSM8K and MATH (even R1-written ones), and DeepSeek-R1 reports few-shot consistently degrades it. An analogue-exemplar step must beat a zero-shot baseline of the same model before it is kept.
agent_test: Run zero-shot, 5-shot, and analogue-exemplar arms on the current model at equal tokens; keep the analogue step only if it beats zero-shot.

claim: Abstracted or curated memory beats verbatim storage and raw retrieval on most tested tasks: Agent Workflow Memory +4.0 step SR over concrete-example retrieval; Dynamic Cheatsheet AIME 2024 Sonnet 50.0 vs full-history 26.7 vs baseline 23.3. But retrieval and memory also lowered strong-model scores in some cells (GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2 to 44.0).
agent_test: At S9 store abstracted lessons (placeholders for specifics) and screen each by a with/without code-checked run.

claim: For agent experience memory, retrieval key matters: task-level similarity beat step-level similarity and random in ExpeL (ALFWorld 59.0% best). No study varied surface text vs abstracted purpose/mechanism vs typed structure, so the best key is unknown.
agent_test: Run a three-arm key test (surface text, abstracted mechanism string, typed slots) on held-out code-checked tasks with matched with/without runs.

claim: LLM-generated ideas lose 1.0 to 1.9 points of reviewer rating after expert execution while human ideas stay flat (Si et al.), and intrinsic self-correction lowers GPT-4 GSM8K from 95.5 to 89.0 (Huang et al.); these are indirect evidence, and no direct test of LLM self-rating of analogue usefulness was found.
agent_test: Score an analogue by matched with/without executed outcome, never by the model's rating.
audit_note: The '169 credited vs 10 real marginal helps' agent-memory audit is not supported by either listed source, and Si et al. measure human-reviewer ratings, not the model's own rating.
claim_before_audit: A model's own rating of an idea or lesson is a weak guide: LLM ideas lose 1.0 to 1.9 rating points after expert execution while human ideas stay flat; intrinsic self-correction lowers GPT-4 GSM8K from 95.5 to 89.0; and outcome-after-retrieval gives 169 credited vs 10 real marginal helps in one audit of agent memory. No direct test of LLM self-rating of analogue usefulness exists.

claim: An explicit abstraction step before solving (step-back) helps weak models more than strong ones (PaLM-2L physics +8.2 over CoT; GPT-4 +1.6 over CoT) and fixes up to 40% of errors while introducing up to 12% new ones. By analogy a 'name the shared structure first' step is expected to matter most for weaker models, but it was not tested on analogy tasks.
agent_test: Test a name-the-shared-structure step on far-analogue items with a code-checked answer; report fixed vs newly broken counts.

claim: No rigorous expert or finished-design test of LLM design-by-analogy was found for 2024 to 2026. Nearest items: a 2026 survey saying such evaluation is lacking, a 32-student counterbalanced AI-ideation experiment with no uniform AI advantage (human-only higher on innovation), and the NLP ideation-execution study.
agent_test: Treat all DbA-LLM gains as unproven until an equal-token, executed-outcome control is run.
audit_note: Negative-search claim cannot be verified; all three cited items exist and match (survey gap statement is in its discussion, not the abstract).
